title: US initial jobless claims, week ending Jun 20 2026
question: What will the U.S. Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration first report as the seasonally adjusted advance initial unemployment insurance claims count for the week ending June 20, 2026?
resolutionSource: U.S. Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report
resolutionRule: Resolve to the advance seasonally adjusted initial claims figure for the week ending June 20, 2026 in the first U.S. Department of Labor ETA Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report released for that week, expected at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on Thursday, June 25, 2026. Use the first-print headline count in persons, not later revisions, FRED backfills, or unadjusted claims.
drivers: Recent claims moved up from the May trough but remain low by historical standards
Late-May and June school-calendar seasonality can create noisy weekly changes
Continuing claims and insured unemployment rate are stable rather than signaling an abrupt layoff break
Year-ago comparable June claims were higher than current readings

reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference-class: weekly initial claims are noisy but mean-reverting at a 1-3 week horizon. Recent 2026 levels cluster near 210,000-229,000, while the same June window in 2025 ran 231,000-246,000, so a central forecast should stay near the latest value but not fully extrapolate the late-May jump.

Recent 5-week average using DOL/FRED values is (212,000 + 210,000 + 212,000 + 225,000 + 229,000) / 5 = 217,600. The latest 4-week average is 219,000. A same-season 2025 anchor for week ending June 21 is 236,000, but current June 6 is 17,000 below the 2025 comparable 246,000, implying an adjusted seasonal anchor near 219,000. I blend latest 229,000, recent-average 218,000, and seasonal-adjusted 219,000, then allow for another school-calendar noisy week to set the point at 226,000.

Counter-consideration: the June 6 unadjusted actual claims jumped by 39,713 and state moves in California, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Texas, and other large states show timing noise that could persist into the June 20 week; this raises upside risk even though the seasonally adjusted series may mean-revert.

For an 80% interval, recent weekly moves include +13,000, +4,000, -25,000, and +15,000 over spring 2026, and June school-season volatility can add several thousand more. Around a 226,000 point, a practical 80% range is roughly -21,000/+24,000, giving 205,000 to 250,000.
